case.summary: Transaction 3503878 for $99.92 online was flagged by the model with a score of 0.9 as part of a seven-transaction episode totaling $816.62 occurring between 2016-11-28 and 2016-12-04 across multiple billing regions. The device profile for this transaction is marked new to the account and is shared with account C07727. The account shows a history of geographic and channel diversity with 248 transactions across 33 regions, but carries three prior confirmed-fraud cases (two out-of-region use, one card-not-present). Case memory identified eight structurally similar closed cases retrieved by shared device, matching pattern, and matching region, all eight of which were confirmed fraud with no false alarms, including cases with account takeover patterns and exposures ranging from $98.01 to $1835.06. The assessment flags account takeover as the suspected pattern with fraud probability 0.62. This is genuine fraud with high confidence. The evidence supporting this conclusion is strong: the device sharing with another account, the multiple prior fraud cases on this customer, the uniform confirmation rate of similar cases in memory, and the episode pattern all point to account compromise. The one mild limitation is that the assessment itself rates confidence as uncertain, though this appears to reflect the inherent ambiguity in distinguishing account takeover from legitimate but unusual activity rather than contradicting the case evidence.
